DEF-160.title: detectFeedFormat ignores the image_url/icon_url push-material aliases validatePushMaterial accepts
DEF-160.source: packages/core/format-detect.js (detectFeedFormat, hasImage/hasClick predicate, line 212) vs packages/core/rules-feed.js (validatePushMaterial alias table, line 164-214)
DEF-160.expected: A push material recognized and cleanly validated under its documented image_url/icon_url alias names (Kadam contract, formats-feeds map §1.1/§1.2) also receives the push format tag from detectFormat, the same way it would under the bare image/icon keys.
DEF-160.actual: The exact reviewed deviations are pinned separately for each case and layer; successful or unrelated findings are not admitted as gaps.
notes: Normative assertions were authored from the documented Kadam field contract (tests/corpus/pairs/push/push-kadam-icon-notice.json; formats-feeds map §1.1/§1.2) before execution; known-gap signatures document observed failures only, not expected-output snapshots.

Distinct from DEF-107 (no decoder for the vendor's GET-URL request): both cases here are response-only and never exercise a URL decoder at all — the sole deviation is the missing format tag on an otherwise cleanly-validated, zero-finding response.

push-x-kadam-array-alias-mixed uses the same image_url/icon_url aliases on two of its three materials but is NOT listed here: detectFeedFormat unions tags across every array element, and that case's first material uses bare image/icon keys, so the array as a whole is still tagged push. The gap is confirmed isolated to the single-object/all-aliased-array shape.

DEF-161.title: Array dispatch forces push-material field names onto a different vendor's documented single-bid shape
DEF-161.source: packages/core/rules-feed.js (validateFeedResponse, unconditional Array.isArray branch, line 49-51) vs https://docs.richads.com/ssp/telegram-native.html (RichAds Telegram SSP bare-array response)
DEF-161.expected: An array element whose keys match a documented single-bid vendor shape (RichAds: title/description/image/notification_url/link/bid_price, sources-vendor map §2a) is validated against that shape's own field contract, not force-fit through the push-material alias table; RichAds documents no id field at all and spells its price and win-notify fields bid_price/notification_url, neither of which validatePushMaterial's alias table recognizes.
DEF-161.actual: The exact reviewed deviations are pinned separately for each case and layer; successful or unrelated findings are not admitted as gaps.
notes: Verified empirically: validateFeedResponse checks Array.isArray(arrOrObj) before ever calling detectSingleBidShape, so wrapping an otherwise bidprice-shaped object ({notification_url, bid_price, ...}) in a bare array is enough by itself to flip Core from what would have been validateBidPriceFeed (correct dispatch for a single such object) to the push-material validator (wrong field contract) — the object's own keys never change, only the array wrapper does.

detectFormat still tags this array push correctly (RichAds happens to use bare image/link/title keys, which detectFeedFormat's hasImage/hasClick/hasTitle test does recognize), so this gap is scoped to field-level false positives (id_required, bid_required, nurl_recommended) only, not format detection — kept distinct from DEF-160 for that reason.
